searches.note: Twenty seven searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's; one left unspent. Fifteen were restricted to a primary body's or a house's own domain (tenutasanguido.com twice, bolgheridoc.com twice, ornellaia.com twice with masseto.com once beside it, collemassariwines.it twice, lemacchiole.it four times, tuarita.it three times) and are read as primary through their summaries. The two shared searches settled the consorzio's history and rules (the decree of 1 August 1983 for white and rosé, red wine from 1994, the Superiore's two years with one in oak, Syrah and Sangiovese each up to half) and asked after the Bolgheri Rosso rules before 2011, which one secondary account alone gave. No WebFetch was tried. Every record was tested; no fact that rests on no source was kept.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the dates and the people, then to the making and the rules, then to the story beats the author had on one account; a fact the Codex library states stood on the library unless a search contradicted it.
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a claim rested on one account it was hedged as that account, turned into the typical case or cut.

Sources whose title or address names a living person (a wine wiki under a writer's first name, the critics' and bloggers' pieces reprinted on the Tua Rita site, a newsletter under a writer's name) were read in the results but never cited.

tested: Mario Incisa della Rocchetta: born in Rome in 1899 (Visit Tuscany, with the estate's history in the same search summary; Wein.plus gives 1899 to 1983), died 1983 (the author's FINE+RARE and Decanter, and Wein.plus): confirmed, named with both dates.

The planting: the estate dates the first Cabernet to the early 1940s below the Castiglioncello fortress (its denomination page) and to 1944 (its Sassicaia page); the cuttings from the Salviati of Migliarino (the estate); its history gives mixed first plantings and the Cabernet selection between 1960 and 1968: the year kept, the vineyard now with Cabernet among its vines.
The Lafite story: Wikipedia gives the son's denial (cuttings from a friend's estate near Pisa), FINE+RARE and Vinfolio tell it as one story among three: told as a story, the denial kept.

The private years and the first sale: the estate kept the wine for family and friends until 1967, the 1968 its first commercial vintage, released in 1971 (its wines and 1968 pages); no source gave 1945 as the first wine, Wikipedia gives 1948: the 1945 cut.

Tachis: credited with temperature controlled fermentation after the alliance with Antinori; French Tronçais barriques are dated to the 1977 vintage in several accounts, and one keeps Slavonian barriques until 1982: the barriques taken from his sentence.

The 1978 tasting: a blind tasting of Cabernets in London organised by Decanter, 33 wines from 11 countries (FINE+RARE, Vinfolio, Tasting Book, Decanter's own story of Sassicaia): confirmed; the winning vintage stays out, as the author had it.

The rules: at least four fifths Cabernet Sauvignon with other red grapes of Tuscany, two years from 1 January after the harvest of which eighteen months in barrels of no more than 225 litres, yield seven tonnes a hectare (the production code); a sub-zone of Bolgheri DOC from 1994 and a DOC of its own in December 2013 (the consorzio): confirmed, the barrel size corrected.

The vineyards and making: 100 to 400 metres facing west and south west (the 2020 and 2021 sheets; 80 to 400 in 1992), steel at controlled temperature, maceration of ten to fifteen days by variety (2015), malolactic in steel (2007, 2013, 2020), about two years in French barriques, 40 to 45 per cent new in 2020 and 2021 (the sheets); soils of limestone and marl with stones, partly clay (VinePair and the estate's sheets in the same search): confirmed, the per parcel and wild yeast clause cut.
The house rules: nobody living named; no price or score (the 1978 tasting is told as a tasting won, no mark given); no superlative; British spelling; no dash.

tested: Founding and first wine: established in 1981, Ornellaia launched with the 1985 (the house's history page): confirmed with the library.

Tchelistcheff: 1901 to 1994 (Wein.plus, beside the author's Wikipedia and Wine History Project), consulting from 1981 and guiding the Merlot onto the blue clay of the Masseto hill (Wein.plus, FINE+RARE, Vinfolio, Decanter's Ornellaia profile): confirmed, now named with his dates.

Masseto: bottles of every vintage since 1986 kept at the estate (masseto.com); the 1986 bottled as Merlot dell'Ornellaia as an experiment never released by FINE+RARE and Vinfolio, the 1987 the first under the name of Masseto: the 1986 no longer sold.

Ownership: Mondavi in from November 1999 (Wikipedia) or 2000 (Decanter), partners with the Frescobaldi by 2002, Constellation buying Mondavi and the Frescobaldi taking the remaining half in 2005 under their contract (Decanter's news, Wikipedia); one account gives the founder's last half sold to the Frescobaldi in 2003: the story holds for all of them.

The making: steel, with concrete on the 2016 and 2020 sheets and not on those of 2010 and 2015; about a week of fermentation and fifteen days on the skins; malolactic mostly in barrique, 70 per cent new; blended after a year and returned for six months (eight in 2008 and 2016), eighteen to twenty months in all; twelve months in bottle (the sheets): confirmed, concrete dated to later vintages.
The rules: Bolgheri Superiore two years from 1 January after the harvest, one in oak (the consorzio's code and wines page): confirmed for the classification and the label.
Le Serre Nuove as Bolgheri DOC Rosso: the house's 2022 sheet: confirmed.

The house rules: nobody living named (the founder is a younger son of the Antinori family); the present ownership not stated, the purchase of 2005 told as history; no superlative; British spelling; no dash.

tested: Founding and first vintage: founded in 1977, the first vintage 1982, a blend of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Sangiovese (the estate on the ColleMassari site, Vino Joy, Club Oenologique); The Buyer gives a Sangiovese majority in 1982 and Merlot only from 1995; the 1982 a table wine (Club Oenologique): kept as the estate's account.
The second estate: the second winery of Bolgheri after Sassicaia or its second oldest estate (two secondary accounts, the estate's own words): confirmed as told.

Vermentino: the Trebbiano of the farm pulled out and Vermentino planted from 1986, the estate's claim to be the first in Bolgheri (the estate, Club Oenologique, Vino Joy): confirmed, the first kept as the house's own account.
ColleMassari in 2002 (the estate; the founder sold in 2002 by the trade accounts): confirmed.

Site and making: 100 to 200 metres; spontaneous fermentation in open conical oak vats of seven hectolitres, punched down by hand, long macerations; eighteen months in French barriques from new to second use; twelve months in bottle (the estate's pages and the 2015 sheet): confirmed; the blend about two thirds Cabernet Sauvignon (65 per cent with 20 Merlot and 15 Sangiovese on the house's page): confirmed.

The rules: the DOC of 1983 for white and rosé, red from 1994; the Superiore two years, one in oak; Syrah and Sangiovese each up to half in the code as it stands (the consorzio's history, code and wines page); Wikipedia gives an older rule of up to seven tenths Sangiovese: the story no longer ties the half to 1994.
The house rules: the founder and the buyer of 2002 described, never named; no superlative (the library's "among the better whites" not repeated); British spelling; no dash.

tested: Founding: 1983 by Eugenio Campolmi and his wife (Wine Spectator, the Wine Scholar Guild, Grand Cru Wijnen); one account gives a first vineyard in 1975 and another a takeover of 1981: the house's 1983 kept with the library.
Eugenio Campolmi: died on 14 July 2002, aged forty (Decanter's report of his death, Chateau Monty); birth year not found: kept with the year of his death.

Paleo: first made in 1989 of Cabernet Sauvignon with a tenth of Sangiovese; the 1995 the same, the 1996 with a touch of Cabernet Franc, the 2000 seven tenths Cabernet Sauvignon and three tenths Cabernet Franc; Cabernet Franc alone from 2001; named for a wild herb of the coast (the house's vintage sheets): confirmed, so every blend before 2001 was led by Cabernet Sauvignon and the question's key stands.
Messorio and Scrio: both first made in 1994 (the house's pages, Wine Spectator, trade guides): confirmed, Scrio added to the story.
The label: Toscana IGT on the house's later sheets; a search summary gives Bolgheri Rosso Superiore DOC on the 1995 sheet: left open.

The parcels and soils: Casa Nuova, Vignone and Ulivino on the later sheets, planted between 1998 and 2016; the 2001 from Contessine (1983) and Puntone (1994); Casa Nuova clay with a skeleton of sandstone, Vignone on limestone rock, Ulivino clay and sand (the vineyards page): confirmed, the soils added.

The making: 20 to 40 days in concrete on the 2018 and newest sheets; 16 months all new (2001), 14 months three quarters new (2008), 20 months seven tenths new (2013), 19 and 18 months all new (2016, 2018), the newest sheet 16 months in new barrels, conical wooden vats and a stoneware amphora: the making rewritten to the range.
The house rules: the widow and the sons described, never named; the library's benchmark not repeated; no superlative; British spelling; no dash.

tested: Founding: 1984 at Notri in Suvereto, in the Colline Metallifere, by the couple who give the estate its name, the name the founder's given name and surname reversed (the house's home and story pages, the Wine Scholar Guild): confirmed.

The motive: to live close to nature and farm the land (the house's story page; WineNews in Italian: to live in contact with nature); one account gives a country home for retirement; no source mentions olive oil: the olive oil cut.
Giusto di Notri first made in 1992 and Redigaffi from two barriques of Merlot set apart in 1994, named for a stream by the estate (the house's pages, Bibenda on the house's site): confirmed.
The 2000 vintage as the breakthrough: every account read; its fame is a critic's mark, left out as a score; the family's dating of the turn found in no source read: cut.
The founder's partner died in 2010 (the house's story page and the Wine Scholar Guild): confirmed, kept described.

The wine: Toscana Merlot IGT; markedly clay soil with a good share of pebbles, cordon spur at 8,500 vines a hectare; ten days in temperature controlled steel and twenty five more on the skins; eighteen to twenty months in new French barriques; bottled in summer and rested months in bottle (the 2019 and newest sheets): confirmed; the house serves it at 15 to 18 degrees Celsius.
The house rules: nobody living named (the founder, her daughter and the family described); no score (the critic's mark of the 2000 left out); no superlative; British spelling; no dash.
